source: references/knowledge/heuristics.md (H1–H10 and the ISO 9241-110 crosswalk), references/methods/cognitive-walkthrough.md (CW-Q1…Q4), references/knowledge/ai-features.md (HAX-G1…G18). Names and guidelines are paraphrased as in those files.

nielsen.name: Visibility of system status
nielsen.means: People can always tell what the system is doing and what just happened, because feedback arrives soon enough to be connected to their action.

nielsen.name: Match between the system and the real world
nielsen.means: The interface uses the words, concepts and order its users know from their own world and work, rather than the organisation's or the code's vocabulary, and controls relate to their effects the way physical things do.

nielsen.name: User control and freedom
nielsen.means: People take wrong turns, so every state offers an obvious way back or out, and actions can be reversed without a long detour.

nielsen.name: Consistency and standards
nielsen.means: A word, look or action means the same thing everywhere in the product (internal consistency), and the product follows the conventions people know from the platform and from other products (external consistency).

nielsen.name: Error prevention
nielsen.means: Design so that mistakes are hard to make: remove the conditions that cause them, constrain input to what is valid, and check consequential actions before they take effect.

nielsen.name: Recognition rather than recall
nielsen.means: What people need to act is in front of them or one step away; they never have to carry a value, choice or instruction in their head from one screen to the next.

nielsen.name: Flexibility and efficiency of use
nielsen.means: The interface serves newcomers and frequent users at once: experienced people get faster routes (accelerators, defaults, saved settings) that newcomers can ignore.

nielsen.name: Aesthetic and minimalist design
nielsen.means: Each screen carries only what serves the task at hand, because every irrelevant or rarely needed element draws attention away from the ones that matter. The heuristic is about relevance and focus, not about a flat or sparse style.

nielsen.name: Help users recognize, diagnose, and recover from errors
nielsen.means: When something fails, the message says in plain words what went wrong and what to do next, sits where the problem is, and keeps the person's work so recovery is quick.

nielsen.name: Help and documentation
nielsen.means: The best interface needs no manual. Where explanation is unavoidable, it is easy to find, appears where the question arises, stays on the task and gives concrete steps.

iso_9241_110.name: Suitability for the user’s tasks
iso_9241_110.note: No Nielsen counterpart; cite USE-08 for task suitability (heuristics.md §2.3).

iso_9241_110.name: User engagement
iso_9241_110.note: No Nielsen counterpart; cite the nearest heuristic as primary and add ISO 9241-110 #7 as a corroborating label (heuristics.md §2.3).

cw_questions.question: Will the user try to achieve the right effect?
Will the user notice that the correct action is available?
Will the user associate the correct action with the effect they want?
If the correct action is performed, will the user see that progress is being made?

hax.guideline: Say what the system can do
Say how well it can do it
Pick the moment from the context
Show what is relevant to the current context
Follow the social norms of the users' setting
Make it quick to call up
Make it quick to dismiss or ignore
Do less, or ask, when uncertain
Explain why it did what it did
Say how user actions shape later behaviour
Tell users when the system changes
